rows.description: I look down on a slower colleague and roll my eyes in meetings. I see that contempt says more about my stress and pride than their worth, and I choose to help or set clear expectations instead of mocking.

rows.description: A colleague makes remarks or contact that make me uncomfortable and I doubt whether it is serious. It is, and it is not my fault. I say a clear no, note dates and details, and use HR, a committee, or a trusted senior.

rows.description: A colleague covered for me during a family emergency and I feel indebted. I thank them sincerely and return the favour at the right time; a workplace of mutual help is worth more than any single task.

rows.subtopic: Being idolised or hated by juniors
